about: The one sentence that says what each molecule of the Everyday topic is, and where in its PubChem record the statement behind it was read. Each record was read through PubChem's public REST services with fetch-pubchem-notes.mjs: the record descriptions (PUG REST, compound/cid/<cid>/description) and, where a description does not say what a person knows the substance by, one section of the record (PUG View, data/compound/<cid>?heading=<heading>). Nothing that was read is kept. `found` says in this project's words what the passage establishes; `source` is the depositor PubChem names beside the passage. The sentences are this project's own: none repeats six words running of a passage. They say what a substance is or where a person meets it; none gives advice on health or on amounts.
citedAs: Each sentence is stored in the molecule's file under its record's source (pubchem-cid-<cid>), which links the record. Indigo's is the exception, and its sentence names the other record in its own words.

notes.note: The stimulant in coffee and tea.
notes.found: a purine alkaloid that is in tea and coffee by nature; among its roles, a stimulant of the central nervous system.

notes.note: A medicine for pain, fever and inflammation.
notes.found: a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug; among its roles, a non-narcotic analgesic and an antipyretic.

notes.note: A medicine for pain and fever.
notes.found: named paracetamol there; among its roles, a non-narcotic analgesic and an antipyretic.

notes.note: An anti-inflammatory medicine, also used against pain and fever.
notes.found: among its roles, a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug, a non-narcotic analgesic and an antipyretic.

notes.note: A flavouring with the smell of vanilla.
notes.found: ChEBI: among its roles, a flavouring agent. HSDB: its odour is that of vanilla.

notes.note: The form of menthol most common in nature; it smells of peppermint.
notes.found: ChEBI: of the mirror-image forms of menthol, this one is the commonest in nature. HSDB: its odour is that of peppermint.

notes.note: A plant compound with the smell of citrus.
notes.found: ChEBI: a plant metabolite. HSDB: a citrus odour.

notes.note: The compound that gives chili peppers their heat.
notes.source: Toxin and Toxin Target Database (T3DB); Haz-Map
notes.found: T3DB: what is active in chili peppers, and put in food to make it spicy. Haz-Map: the pungent component of plants of the capsicum species.

notes.note: A flavouring with the smell of cinnamon.
notes.found: ChEBI: among its roles, a flavouring agent. HSDB: a strong odour of cinnamon.

notes.note: Vitamin C, also added to food as an antioxidant.
notes.found: it is a vitamin C; among its roles, a food antioxidant.

notes.note: An alkaloid of the cacao plant, found in chocolate.
notes.found: a purine alkaloid that comes from the cacao plant and is in chocolate.

notes.note: The form of nicotine found in nature, in the tobacco plant.
notes.found: the mirror-image form of nicotine that occurs in nature, isolated from Nicotiana tabacum (the tobacco plant).

notes.note: An ester with the smell of bananas.
notes.found: ChEBI: an acetate ester. HSDB: a fruity odour, of banana among others (one entry says pear).

notes.note: An ester with the smell of wintergreen, used as a flavouring.
notes.found: ChEBI: salicylic acid's methyl ester; among its roles, a flavouring agent. HSDB: the odour of wintergreen.

notes.note: A flavouring and fragrance with the smell of bitter almonds.
notes.found: ChEBI: among its roles, a flavouring agent and a fragrance. HSDB: an odour like that of the oil of bitter almonds.

notes.note: A compound with an earthy smell.
notes.where: record description (read in the whole record; the description request returns ChEBI's alone, and the record has no Odor section)
notes.found: an earthy-smelling compound. Nothing read says that it is the smell of rain, so the sentence does not.

notes.note: A neurotransmitter of the brain.
notes.found: one of the brain's neurotransmitters of the catecholamine kind.

notes.note: A neurotransmitter found in the human body.
notes.found: among its roles, a neurotransmitter and a human metabolite.

notes.note: The "fight or flight" hormone, made by the adrenal glands.
notes.found: a hormone that the adrenal glands secrete and that brings about the fight-or-flight response.

notes.note: A dye. PubChem keeps that name on another record, CID 10215, which draws another form of the same molecule.
notes.where: record description and section Uses of CID 10215; the properties of both records
notes.found: The record whose structure the library uses (CID 5318432, two C=O and two N-H) has no title, no description and no synonyms section. The record titled Indigo (CID 10215) has the same formula with one hydrogen on an oxygen in place of a nitrogen, a tautomer; ChEBI's description there names it indigo dye, and its Uses section lists a cosmetic colorant. Nothing read says that it is blue or what it dyes, so the sentence does not.

notes.note: Used in finding the octane number of a fuel.
notes.source: EPA Hazardous Air Pollutants; Hazardous Substances Data Bank (HSDB)
notes.found: used in determining the octane numbers of fuels.

notes.note: An artificial sweetener.
notes.found: in common use as an artificial sweetener.

otherNotes.rests: NIST CCCBDB, experimental geometry page for nitric acid (casno 7697372), read 2026-10-09 with fetch-cccbdb.mjs: rNO 1.406 to the oxygen that carries the hydrogen, 1.211 and 1.199 to the other two (Cox and Riveros 1965).
The lengths of their own cited geometry (geometry.json).
The SMILES of each PubChem record, in pubchem.json, for how PubChem draws it; expected.json, convention octet-forms, for the choice.

The sentence the spec gives every zwitterion (section 6.1). It was not read again for these two: their record descriptions (ChEBI) say only what a zwitterion is: the amino acid with the proton of its acid group moved to its nitrogen.

ids: every added molecule that says "One conformer of many."
otherNotes.rests: PubChem's own count of conformers for the record, more than one (conformerCount3D in pubchem.json).
